CSV TOWN FLAG: this temple is NOT in Tiruchirappalli town - it is in SRIRANGAM town, on Srirangam island between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers (~9-10 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction). The Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam is the largest temple complex in India and is listed as the biggest functioning Hindu temple in the world (~156 acres). It is the FIRST of the 108 Divya Desams dedicated to Vishnu and one of the self-manifested Svayam Vyakta Kshetras, glorified in the Thiviya Pirabandham of the Alwar saints (6th-9th c.). Legend: Rama gave the reclining Vishnu idol to Vibhishana, who set it down on the Kaveri bank; it refused to move, facing south toward Lanka. The complex has seven concentric prakarams and 21 gopurams, with the southern Rajagopuram at ~237-239.5 ft the tallest temple tower in Asia (completed 1987 after stalling 400+ years). Ramanuja made his monastic home here; the temple follows the Thenkalai tradition of worship (Pancharatra Agama).
